methodologies.name: Yessis 1×20 (Foundational GPP)
methodologies.philosophy: Dr. Michael Yessis's general physical preparation system: high exercise variety, one set of 20 reps per exercise, moderate intensity. Develops all joint actions comprehensively as the entry phase for youth athletes.
methodologies.definition:
FOUNDATIONAL TIER RULES (Yessis 1×20 Phase):
This athlete is learning basic movement patterns. Use the Yessis 1×20 approach:
- Program 15–20 exercises per session, each for 1 SET of 20 REPS.
  This high-exercise, low-set structure develops all joint actions comprehensively.
- Use ONLY bodyweight exercises, resistance bands, and light dumbbells (≤15 lbs per hand).
- Do NOT use barbell exercises (no squat, bench, deadlift with barbell).
- Do NOT use percentage-based loading — use absolute_weight only.
- Rep range: 15–20 reps for all exercises. No sets below 10 reps.
- ONE working set per exercise. The total session volume comes from exercise variety,
  not multiple sets of the same movement.
- Exercise selection should cover ALL major joint actions:
  • Hip hinge (e.g., RDL with light dumbbells, good mornings with band)
  • Knee extension/flexion (e.g., goblet squats, lunges, step-ups)
  • Ankle (e.g., calf raises, single-leg balance)
  • Shoulder push/pull (e.g., push-ups, band pull-aparts, overhead press with light DB)
  • Elbow flexion/extension (e.g., light curls, tricep extensions — for joint health)
  • Spine/core (e.g., planks, dead bugs, bird dogs, pallof press)
- Target technical failure (form breakdown), NOT muscular failure.
  When the athlete can complete 20 reps with perfect form, increase load by 1–2.5 lbs.
- Plateau trigger: if the athlete stalls at the same weight for 2–3 sessions,
  vary the exercise (e.g., swap goblet squat for split squat) before increasing load.
- Sessions should feel moderate — the athlete should leave feeling capable of more.
- Include form_notes on every prescribed set emphasizing technique cues.
- Training frequency: 2–3 sessions per week with the SAME exercises to build
  motor learning through repetition.

methodologies.name: Yessis 1×15 (Intermediate GPP)
methodologies.philosophy: Second Yessis foundational phase. Modest intensity bump from 1×20: light barbell variations introduced for main lifts, but the high-variety, low-set, technique-first structure carries through.
methodologies.definition:
INTERMEDIATE TIER RULES (Yessis 1×15 Phase):
This athlete has demonstrated foundational movement competency. Transition to
the Yessis 1×15 approach — the second foundational phase that introduces
weighted and barbell variations over the 1×20 base:
- Program 12–15 exercises per session, each for 1 SET of 15 REPS.
  Same high-variety, low-set structure as 1×20 with a modest intensity bump.
- Replace bodyweight versions with weighted variations where appropriate
  (e.g., weighted push-up replaces push-up, KB staggered RDL replaces band good
  morning, step-up with knee drive replaces step-up, front squat replaces goblet
  squat).
- May introduce light barbell work for main lifts (front squat, bench press,
  trap bar deadlift, barbell row) with technique-first loading — start with the
  empty bar or light loads and add 2.5–5 lbs only when 15 reps are clean.
- Dumbbells/kettlebells up to ~25–30 lbs per implement are appropriate.
- Do NOT use percentage-based loading — use absolute_weight only.
- Rep range: 15 reps for all exercises (matching the 1×15 phase name and the
  seeded Foundations 1×15 program). No sets below 12 reps.
- ONE working set per exercise remains the standard. Do NOT add additional sets
  unless the coach explicitly requests it for a specific main lift.
- Continue comprehensive joint action coverage — barbell movements supplement,
  they don't replace, the accessory and isolation work.
- Progression increments: 2.5 lbs for dumbbell/kettlebell lifts, 5 lbs for
  barbell lifts when 15 reps are completed with good form for 2 consecutive
  sessions.
- Plateau trigger: if the athlete stalls at the same weight for 2–3 sessions,
  vary the exercise (e.g., swap front squat for a goblet squat variation)
  before pushing the load.
- Target technical failure (form breakdown), NOT muscular failure. Sessions
  should still feel moderate — the intent is durable adaptation over fatigue.
- Include form_notes on barbell lifts emphasizing technique cues.
- Training frequency: 2 sessions per week with the SAME exercises (looping
  format, matching the seeded Foundations 1×15 program).

methodologies.name: Yessis Sport Performance
methodologies.philosophy: Final youth phase. Structured percentage-based programming for youth athletes with solid technique on compound lifts; introduces controlled power-oriented work (Olympic lift variations, jumps, throws).
methodologies.definition:
SPORT PERFORMANCE TIER RULES:
This athlete has solid technique on compound lifts and is ready for
structured percentage-based programming:
- May use percentage-based loading IF the athlete has training maxes set.
  If no training maxes exist, use absolute_weight and note in reasoning
  that TMs should be established.
- Rep range: 5–10 for main lifts, 8–12 for accessories.
- Maximum 5–6 exercises per session, 3–4 working sets for main lifts.
- Can include power-oriented work (box jumps, med ball throws, light
  Olympic lift variations) with controlled volume (2–3 sets of 3–5 reps).
- Progression increments: 5 lbs for upper body, 5–10 lbs for lower body.
- Program periodization: use linear or simple block periodization.
  Undulating periodization only if training age > 12 months.

methodologies.name: Integrative Youth GPP
methodologies.philosophy: Faigenbaum & Myer's Integrative Neuromuscular Training (INT). Multifaceted youth approach combining strength, plyometrics, balance, agility, and coordination — technique before load, variety over intensity. Complementary alternative to Yessis for youth athletes.
methodologies.definition:
INTEGRATIVE YOUTH GPP RULES (INT-grounded):
This athlete trains under a multifaceted youth approach grounded in
Integrative Neuromuscular Training (Faigenbaum & Myer):
- Each session integrates multiple qualities: strength, plyometrics, balance,
  agility, coordination, and fundamental movement skills. Avoid a strength-only
  session structure.
- Rep ranges: 6–15 reps for strength work; 1–3 sets per strength exercise.
  Plyometric/balance/coordination drills are sets-and-reps light; cue intent
  and quality, not volume.
- Equipment: bodyweight, medicine balls, light dumbbells/kettlebells,
  resistance bands, plyo boxes, balance tools, low hurdles. Barbell work
  belongs in the Yessis 1×15 pathway, not here.
- Technique mastery gates load. Progress an exercise's load only after the
  athlete demonstrates clean, repeatable technique at the current weight.
- Each session should cover multiple movement patterns and at least one
  non-strength quality (a jump variation, a balance/agility drill, or a
  coordination/locomotion piece).
- 2–3 sessions per week. Allow at least 48 hours between sessions targeting
  the same muscle groups.
- Target technical failure (form breakdown), NOT muscular failure.
- Include form_notes on every prescribed set emphasizing technique cues.

methodologies.philosophy: Jim Wendler's percentage-based intermediate program. Slow, sustainable progression on four main barbell lifts: squat, bench, deadlift, overhead press. 4-week waves: 5s / 3s / 5/3/1 / deload.
methodologies.definition:
5/3/1 METHODOLOGY:
This athlete trains under Jim Wendler's 5/3/1 intermediate program.
- Train four main barbell lifts: Squat, Bench Press, Deadlift, Overhead Press.
- 4-week mesocycle waves keyed off a Training Max (TM) set at 85–90% of the
  athlete's true 1RM. Increment TM weekly only if the prior cycle's AMRAP set
  cleared 1+ rep over target.
- Main-lift waves (sets × reps × percentage of TM):
  • Week 1 (5s):   5×65, 5×75, 5+×85
  • Week 2 (3s):   3×70, 3×80, 3+×90
  • Week 3 (5/3/1): 5×75, 3×85, 1+×95
  • Week 4 (deload): 5×40, 5×50, 5×60
  The final "+" set is AMRAP — emit reps: null so the athlete logs the actual.
- Accessories: 2–4 per session, hypertrophy-focused (sets of 8–15), volume
  chosen by the assistance template the coach selects (BBB, FSL, jokers, etc.).
- Loading: use percentage-based loading against the TM for main lifts.
- Round all calculated weights down to the nearest 5 lbs (or 2.5 kg).
- Rest periods: 3–5 minutes between main-lift work sets; 60–120 seconds for
  accessories.
- Include RPE guidance on accessories where appropriate.

methodologies.name: 5/3/1 Boring But Big
methodologies.philosophy: 5/3/1 with a high-volume hypertrophy supplement: 5 sets of 10 reps of the main lift at 50–70% TM after the 5/3/1 work sets. Adds size on top of the 5/3/1 strength base.
methodologies.definition:
5/3/1 BORING BUT BIG METHODOLOGY:
This athlete trains under 5/3/1 with the Boring But Big (BBB) hypertrophy
supplement.
- Follow the standard 5/3/1 wave on main lifts (see the 5/3/1 methodology block).
- After the main-lift 5/3/1 work sets, add 5 sets of 10 reps of the same lift
  (or its opposite-pattern pair) at 50–60% TM in cycle 1, progressing to 65–70%
  TM by cycle 3.
- The BBB sets are STRICTLY hypertrophy volume — do not push them to failure.
  Rest 60–90 seconds between BBB sets.
- Accessories are minimized to keep total session volume manageable: 1–2 short
  accessory movements after the BBB sets.
- Loading: percentage-based against TM for both the 5/3/1 and BBB sets.
- This template is volume-heavy; deload week 4 is non-negotiable.

methodologies.name: Greyskull LP
methodologies.philosophy: Phrak's Greyskull Linear Progression. A novice LP: 3 days/week alternating upper/lower main lifts, last set AMRAP, add weight every session. Hits a wall faster than 5/3/1 but maximizes early gains.
methodologies.definition:
GREYSKULL LP METHODOLOGY:
This athlete trains under Phrak's Greyskull Linear Progression.
- 3 sessions per week, alternating A/B day:
  • Day A: Overhead Press 2×5 + 1×AMRAP, Squat 2×5 + 1×AMRAP
  • Day B: Bench Press 2×5 + 1×AMRAP, Deadlift 1×5 + 1×AMRAP
  Add Chin-ups / Pull-ups as a fixed accessory; 1–2 additional accessories OK.
- Loading: ABSOLUTE weight, not percentage. Start at a load the athlete can
  complete all reps with good form, and add 5 lb (upper) / 10 lb (lower) every
  session as long as the AMRAP set hits 5+ reps.
- On the AMRAP set, emit reps: null so the athlete logs the actual reps.
- If the AMRAP set falls below 5 reps two sessions in a row, reset that lift
  10% lower and re-climb. This is the LP "reset" rule.
- Rest 2–3 minutes between main-lift sets; 60–90 seconds for accessories.
- Keep total session length around 45 minutes — this is meant to be repeatable.

methodologies.name: GZCLP
methodologies.philosophy: Cody Lefever's GZCL Linear Progression. A novice LP organized into T1/T2/T3 tiers per session: T1 main lift heavy single + back-off sets, T2 secondary lift moderate volume, T3 accessory hypertrophy.
methodologies.definition:
GZCLP METHODOLOGY:
This athlete trains under Cody Lefever's GZCL Linear Progression (GZCLP).
- 4 sessions per week (A1/B1/A2/B2 rotation). Each session has three tiers:
  • T1 — Main lift: 5×3 then 1+ AMRAP (the "+" set). Add 5 lb upper / 10 lb
    lower after the AMRAP clears 3+ reps.
  • T2 — Secondary compound: 3×10 with a fixed weight. Add weight when 3×10
    is hit; reset rep scheme to 3×8 / 3×6 if stalled, then re-climb.
  • T3 — Accessory: 3×15+ with a fixed weight. Last set is AMRAP; emit
    reps: null. Add weight when AMRAP clears 25 reps.
- T1 and T2 rotate between Squat/Deadlift on lower days and Bench/OHP on
  upper days. Pair so the lift the athlete deadlifts in T1 is the bench
  variant in T2 (or vice versa).
- Loading: ABSOLUTE weight for all three tiers. Stay in 5 lb / 10 lb
  increments. No percentage-based loading.
- On every AMRAP set emit reps: null so the athlete logs the actual.
- Rest: 3–5 minutes after T1 work sets; 90–120 seconds between T2 sets;
  60–90 seconds for T3.

methodologies.name: 5×5 (Linear Progression)
methodologies.philosophy: Classic Bill Starr / StrongLifts-style novice 5×5. 3 days/week alternating two workouts of three main lifts; add weight every session until reset.
methodologies.definition:
5×5 METHODOLOGY:
This athlete trains under a classic Bill-Starr-style 5×5 novice linear
progression.
- 3 sessions per week, alternating A/B workouts:
  • Workout A: Squat 5×5, Bench Press 5×5, Barbell Row 5×5
  • Workout B: Squat 5×5, Overhead Press 5×5, Deadlift 1×5
- All work sets are at the same weight (no warm-up percentages in the prescribed
  set rows; warm-ups are the athlete's responsibility).
- Loading: ABSOLUTE weight. Add 5 lb upper / 5–10 lb lower every session as
  long as all 5×5 are clean. Deadlift adds 10 lb after each successful single.
- If the athlete misses reps two sessions in a row on a lift, deload that lift
  10% and re-climb.
- Rest 3–5 minutes between sets — this volume × intensity needs full recovery.
- One short accessory block (Chin-ups, Dips, abs) is optional but small —
  the 5×5 main lifts are the workout.

methodologies.name: Sarge Athletics Circuit
methodologies.philosophy: Circuit / EMOM-style conditioning + strength density work. Each session opens with EMOM cleans, then 3 rounds of paired-exercise circuit rows mixing carries, throws, sled work, and core stability.
methodologies.definition:
SARGE CIRCUIT METHODOLOGY:
This athlete trains in a Sarge Athletics circuit / EMOM format. The session is
dense, mixed-implement, and conditioning-flavored on top of strength density.

- Structure: Every session opens with EMOM cleans (5×5 power cleans, one set per
  minute), followed by 3 circuit "rows" of paired exercises done for multiple rounds.
- Circuit rows: Each row pairs 2–3 exercises done back-to-back with minimal rest.
  Complete all exercises in the row, then repeat for the prescribed number of rounds
  (typically 3–4 rounds per row).
- Indicate circuit structure via notes: The FIRST set of each row's first exercise
  should include a note like "Circuit Row 1 — complete row then repeat x4 rounds".
  EMOM sets should note "EMOM — 1 set every minute on the minute".
- sort_order: Within a day, EMOM cleans get sort_order 1–5. Each circuit row's
  exercises are interleaved by round (all rounds of one exercise, then all rounds
  of the paired exercise), advancing sort_order sequentially.
- Exercise pairing: Pair opposing movement patterns (push/pull, anterior/posterior)
  or strength + stability (e.g., squat + plank variation).
- Rest periods: Minimal rest within a circuit row (transition time only). Rest
  60–90 seconds between rows. The EMOM format enforces its own rest.
- Mix implements freely: barbells, dumbbells, kettlebells, bodyweight, medicine
  balls, TRX, sleds, battle ropes, carries. Variety is a hallmark of this style.
- Include conditioning elements: battle rope waves, sled work, sprints, burpees,
  medicine ball slams. These should appear as exercises within circuit rows, not
  as separate "cardio" blocks.
- Core work: Integrate core stability (planks, holds, march variations) as paired
  exercises within circuit rows rather than as a separate core block.
- Carries and locomotion: farmer's carries, overhead carries, suitcase marches,
  hover crawls, and similar loaded locomotion work as circuit row exercises.
- Cool-down: Final circuit row may be lower intensity (stretches, mobility,
  lighter movements) as a built-in cool-down.
- Do NOT use percentage-based loading for circuit exercises — use absolute_weight.
  The high-density format makes percentage-based loading inappropriate.
